summary: The manuscript presents four self-contained, elementary, and machine-checked structural theorems resolving unproved algebraic assertions, Magma-only rank-zero barriers, group-law ambiguities, and external descent dependencies in Halbeisen et al. (2026). It provides explicit birational isomorphisms, modular and 2-adic obstruction analysis for elliptic curve ranks, exact group law identities, and constructive Fermat descents. These are verified across three layers: 20 constructive Lean 4 theorems (zero sorry, zero warnings, zero external imports), 16 AST-audited zero-float Python certificates, and 56 adversarial tests.
strengths: Explicit, verified birational isomorphism Psi : Q1 -> E12 with rational inverse and degree-4 descent morphism.
Magma-free complete 2-descent rank-zero proof for the infinite family C = p^k (p = 5 mod 8), A = 2^s, explicitly resolving (5,4) at degree 2.
Exact algebraic group law identity R = +[2]P in both coordinates, resolving previous sign and divisibility ambiguities.
Complete constructive Lean 4 formalization and AST-audited Python verification with zero warnings, zero sorry, and zero floats.
weaknesses: Highly specialized number-theoretic focus with dense algebraic notation.
Complex 2-adic and mod-p valuation case analysis requires rigorous tracking, though fully substantiated by formal proofs.
